summary: Design feasible coverage, contribution and delivery options for informal workers. Explore the five-day course and plan your next step.
lede: Social protection for informal workers involves designing income-support pathways for people with irregular earnings, varied livelihoods or no formal payroll. For social protection officers, programme designers and policy analysts, the task is to turn coverage gaps into feasible scheme and delivery choices. The course builds skills in segmenting workers, comparing contribution or tax-financed options, and planning enrolment, benefit delivery and monitoring using ILO Recommendation No. 202 and CODI as reference frameworks.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess coverage gaps, shape schemes or manage delivery for workers outside standard payroll arrangements. It suits intermediate-level practitioners with some exposure to social protection policy or programme operations.
modules: ILO Recommendation No. 202 and Coverage Gaps
Benefits and Delivery for Informal Workers
prerequisites: Intermediate-level course. Prior exposure to social protection policy, social insurance, social assistance or programme operations is expected. No coding or programming is required; exercises use structured worksheets and may use Excel for simple calculations.
